title: Exponential growth, decay, doubling time, and half-life
section: Chapter 4 Review Questions ▷ Growth proportional to population
terms: exponential growth; exponential decay; proportional rate; growth constant; doubling time; half-life.

A quantity whose instantaneous rate is proportional to its amount satisfies N = kN. The so-

multiply the amount by the same factor, independently of the starting time.
If N(t + T) = aN (t) with a > 0, then k = log a/T . Doubling time is log 2/k for k > 0, and half-
life is log 2/|k| for k < 0. Distinguish a multiplicative increase by a factor a from an additive
increase by a units or a percentage increase of a%. In decay or growth applications, the model
and proportionality assumption determine the exponential law.
A sum of quantities with different decay constants is generally not one exponential, so its half-
time cannot be obtained by averaging individual half-lives. Also a multiplier observed at one
′
fixed time step alone does not imply the differential law N = kN : a positive periodic factor can
preserve that step multiplier while changing the instantaneous rate.

question.text:
Two samples initially have equal amounts and decay exponentially with half-lives 2 and 3 years.
After how many years is the first sample one-fourth the second?
(A) 4 (B) 6 (C) 8 (D) 12 (E) 18

solution.text:
−t/2 −t/3 −t/6 −2
The ratio is 2 /2 = 2 . Set this equal to 1/4 = 2 to get t = 12. Comparing
two amounts uses the difference of their exponential rates, not either sample's individual
half-life.

solution.text:
The periodic factor repeats after one unit, so the third function has the required multiplier.
